newsitem.title: CUBA: Minister suggests bombs caused Havana explosions.
newsitem.headline: Minister suggests bombs caused Havana explosions.

text.p: A Cuban government minister strongly suggested two loud explosions that rocked two central Havana hotels within minutes of each other on Saturday were caused by bombs.

The explosions took place at the Hotel Nacional and the nearby Hotel Capri. Asked by reporters what caused them, Tourism Minister Osmany Cienfuegos, visiting the hotels 30 minutes after the blasts, said: "Obviously they are enemies of ours."

A Danish tourist, Ole Madsen, and several hotel workers said at least three people were injured in the explosion at the Nacional. Madsen told Reuters he saw people on the ground after the explosion and some were bleeding.
At least four ambulances left the hotel about 20 minutes after the explosion, although it was not clear if they were carrying wounded people.
Cienfuegos said there were no injuries in the explosion at the Capri. He said he did not know if there were injuries at the Nacional, since he had not visited there yet.
Witnesses said the explosions, both of which appeared to have hit the hotel lobbies, took place at about 11:25 a.m. (1525 GMT) and 11:30 a.m. (1530 GMT).
